title: Modulating organelle distribution using light-inducible heterodimerization in C. elegans
protocol: Eliminate environmental blue light for animals during culturing and sample preparation.
Store the animals in a box wrapped in aluminum foil to block environmental light.
Use a light source filtered for blue light if room illumination is necessary.
Cover the microscope setup with aluminum foil if needed.
Adjust hardware display settings to omit blue light from monitors.
Insert optical (orange) filters in the light paths of dissection scope and imaging microscope.
Prepare microscope settings for global and local light-induced heterodimerization using a strain where heterodimerization can be easily scored.
Tag ePDZ with a red or far-red fluorophore for visualization without activating LOVpep.
Prepare the sample for imaging while preventing exposure to environmental blue light.
Locate the sample using transmitted light filtered for blue light and acquire a snapshot of the ePDZ fusion protein.
Excite the entire field of view with 488 nm laser light and immediately acquire a second snapshot of the ePDZ fusion protein.
Leave the sample on the microscope for approximately 5 minutes, shielding it from all environmental light to obtain a dark-state condition.
Acquire a third snapshot of the mobile ePDZ fusion protein under the dark-state condition.
Compare the snapshots to determine if unintended light-induced heterodimerization occurs during sample preparation.
Quantify the signal intensities of the ePDZ fusion protein outside and inside the area where the LOVpep fusion protein is localized.
Use the minimal amount of laser power required for LOVpep activation.
Use an excitation power of 2 iterations of 0.1–0.01 μW 488 nm laser light with a pixel dwell time of 8 μs every 2–5 seconds during experiments.
Maintain this power level to recruit ePDZ-mCherry to membrane-bound PH-LOV.
Set up a dark-state, non-activated sample for time-lapse experiment.
Excite a region of interest with 488 nm laser between every snapshot acquisition.
Mix different intensities, pixel dwell times, iterations, and time intervals for the 488 nm laser excitation.
Aim for lower power settings and shorter pixel dwell time to avoid cytotoxicity.
Increase number of iterations if needed to achieve light activation.
Find lowest/shortest settings compatible with experiments showing ePDZ relocation.
Include a negative control expressing only the ePDZ fusion construct.
No relocation or phenotype should be observed in negative control using tested settings.
Process time-lapse images after acquisition to reduce background noise.
Segment activated organelle or structure for signal quantification if necessary.
Calculate the ratio of fluorescence intensity inside the activated region of interest to the intensity in an equivalent size region outside the area of activation.
Determine the maximum intensity ratio and the activation half-life from this analysis.
With these results, determine the minimal amount of power needed to achieve light-induced activation.
Optional: Assess how much light-induced heterodimerization occurs surrounding or outside the area of activation and its impact on the experiment.
Critical: Repeat steps (a)–(g) periodically using a reference strain to calibrate laser power for local activation.
Use the minimal amount of power for light-induced activation.
Repeat the procedure with the LOVpep and ePDZ fusion constructs.
Determine if continuous, transient, or pulsed light-induced activation is needed.
Use continuous light activation to trap mitochondria at the cell membrane when necessary.
Use pulsed activation to explore how organelles recover from light-induced mislocalization when necessary.
Prepare C. elegans zygotes for particle tracking analysis.
Treat zygotes with spd-2 RNAi to prevent mitochondrial streaming towards the future posterior side.
Activate LOVpep using a 488 nm laser line at an intensity of 0.01% and a pixel dwell time of 8 ms.
Start activation at time zero and apply in between each time point, maintaining a 2-second interval.
Perform tracking analysis in the same area where activating light was used for zygotes with activation.
Conduct tracking analysis in a comparable region for zygotes without activation.
Carry out photoactivation between every image acquisition.
Perform light-induced heterodimerization experiments
Using the settings for 488 nm light-induced activation determined in step 6, set up your imaging parameters.
Locate the sample of interest using transmitted light that has been filtered for blue light.
Acquire global light-induced heterodimerization images similar to acquiring GFP images.
Expose only the region of interest (ROI) with a 488 nm laser to achieve local light-induced heterodimerization.
Determine if the light-induced heterodimerization of LOVpep and ePDZ has the desired effect on organelle relocation.
Use particle tracking analysis of the mitochondrial signal to assess if local activation of membrane LOVpep effectively traps mitochondria labeled with ePDZ in the activated area.
Quantify organelle redistribution dynamics by comparing changes in total intensity in the activated and non-activated areas.
